evidence.text: Reason for referral: Evaluation of a newly heard heart murmur.

Findings: Sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm. Normal axis. PR interval 197 ms, QRS 105 ms, QTc
415 ms.
Impression: Sinus bradycardia, otherwise normal tracing.
Most recent echo showed an ejection fraction of 60%.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at
35%. Mild mitral regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Moderately reduced left ventricular systolic function.

LIPID PANEL
Total Cholesterol: 165 mg/dL
LDL Cholesterol: 63 mg/dL
HDL Cholesterol: 57 mg/dL
Triglycerides: 227 mg/dL (H)

BASIC METABOLIC PANEL
Sodium: 142 mmol/L
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L
Chloride: 101 mmol/L
CO2: 27 mmol/L
BUN: 13 mg/dL
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL
Glucose: 170 mg/dL (H)

Discharge medications:
Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily
Metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily
Levothyroxine 50 mcg by mouth once daily

EXAM:
General: welll appearing, no distress.
Neck: supple, no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs: faint bibasilar crackles.
Extremities: trace ankle edema.
